note: Follows 2.2 (levels, sublevels, orbitals) and sets up 2.4 (valence electrons, ions). Notation convention (PROVISIONAL until Matt confirms): filling order, e.g. [Ar] 4s^{2} 3d^{6}, written with true superscript runs ^{...}. Required through Kr (Z = 36), PROVISIONAL scope. Cr and Cu are the only exceptions taught. Every configuration and orbital diagram on these slides, and every configuration in the speaker notes, is checked by scripts/build_diagram_u02_s02.3_configurations.py. 50-minute period; the last 5 minutes are cleanup/reset.

fields.headline:
2.3
Electron
Configurations
fields.subhead: Write configurations and orbital diagrams through krypton, and catch mistakes in them.

imageSubjects.section: a long row of numbered wooden mail slots in a dim hallway, a few holding envelopes

slides.notes: PROVISIONAL scope: required through Kr (Z = 36), per the content brief; Matt to confirm. Period 5 and beyond (Mo, Ag, Au) are not taught on these slides and are not checked in the build script. PROVISIONAL notation: configurations are written in filling order, e.g. [Ar] 4s^2 3d^6, not energy order. Image prompt (section slot): a long row of numbered wooden mail slots in a dim hallway, a few holding envelopes.

fields.headline: Where Are Oxygen's Electrons?
fields.subhead: The periodic table gives you the count: 8. Today you write where each one sits.
fields.keyq: Oxygen has 8 electrons. Do all 8 have the same energy?

imageSubjects.concept: an apartment building at dusk with a few lit windows on different floors

slides.notes: Hook. Ask: do all 8 electrons have the same energy? Let them guess; the slides answer it (no). Z = 8 comes from the periodic table. Image prompt (concept slot): an apartment building at dusk with a few lit windows on different floors.

fields.headline: Reading an Electron Configuration
fields.subhead: Take 2p^{4} apart one piece at a time.
fields.k1_b:
The big number in front.

2p^{4} is in level 2.
fields.k2_b:
The letter: s, p, d, or f.

2p^{4} is in the p sublevel.
fields.mustwrite: A configuration lists where the electrons sit. Ground state means the lowest-energy arrangement.

imageSubjects.aside: a printed periodic table with oxygen's cell circled in pencil

slides.notes: Say it aloud: two-p-four. Level 2, p sublevel, 4 electrons. Ground state = lowest-energy arrangement; every configuration today is a ground state unless the slide says otherwise. Image prompt (aside slot): a printed periodic table with oxygen's cell circled in pencil.

fields.headline: The Order Electrons Fill In
fields.subhead: Read each arrow from top right to bottom left, then start the next arrow.
fields.a1_b: The lowest-energy open orbital fills first.
fields.a3_b: 4s fills before 3d, in K and Ca.

slides.notes: Walk each arrow top right to bottom left. We need the order through 5p: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p 5s 4d 5p. Say it as: 4s fills before 3d in neutral K and Ca. Do not say 4s is always lower than 3d (once 3d holds electrons it sits lower; that is S2.4, ions).

fields.headline: Pauli: Two per Orbital, Opposite Spins
fields.subhead: Up and down arrows are spin labels, not electrons orbiting opposite ways.
fields.a1_b: One orbital holds at most 2 electrons.
fields.a2_b: If there are two, their spins are opposite.
fields.a3_b: Two per orbital, not two per sublevel.

slides.notes: Spin up and down are labels, not literal rotation. Common mix-up: two per orbital, not two per sublevel (a p sublevel has 3 orbitals and holds 6).

fields.headline: Hund's Rule: Singles Before Pairs
fields.subhead: Equal-energy orbitals, like the three 2p boxes, each get one electron first.
fields.a1_b: Singles first, all pointing the same way.
fields.a2_b: Its 2p^{3} is three single electrons: 3 unpaired.

slides.notes: Figure: N in 2p. Correct = three singles, spins parallel. Wrong = one pair, one single, one empty box. Equal-energy orbitals are called degenerate. Electrons spread out first because sharing an orbital costs repulsion.

fields.headline: Reading an Orbital Diagram
fields.subhead: One box per orbital. Nitrogen has 7 electrons, so 7 arrows.
fields.a2_b: Draw the up arrow first in every box.
fields.a3_b: The raised number counts the arrows.

slides.notes: N has 7 electrons so 7 arrows: 2 + 2 + 3. Convention: draw the up arrow first in every box, and the label's raised number counts the arrows.

fields.headline: Writing a Configuration
fields.subhead: The same four steps, for every element.
fields.s1_b: Atomic number is the electron count.
fields.s4_b: The raised numbers must total Z.

imageSubjects.band: a periodic table wall chart photographed at a shallow angle

slides.notes: Four steps, every element. Caps: s 2, p 6, d 10, f 14. Always check that the sum equals Z. Image prompt (band slot): a periodic table wall chart photographed at a shallow angle.

fields.headline: Example: Oxygen
fields.subhead: Copy the setup, not just the answer.
fields.problem: Write the longhand configuration and the orbital diagram for oxygen.
fields.g2_b:
Longhand configuration
Orbital diagram
Unpaired electrons
fields.mustwrite: Always check that the raised numbers add up to Z.

imageSubjects.aside: a small cylinder of oxygen gas with a regulator, on a lab cart

slides.notes: Students copy the setup; the work area stays empty on purpose and is filled live on the board. Answer on the next slide: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4, 2 unpaired. Image prompt (aside slot): a small cylinder of oxygen gas with a regulator, on a lab cart.

fields.headline: Oxygen, Worked
fields.subhead: Order first. Then singles before pairs in the 2p boxes.

slides.notes: Oxygen: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4, 2 + 2 + 4 = 8. The 2p boxes hold one pair and two singles, so 2 unpaired.

fields.headline: Longhand: N, Cl, and Ca
fields.subhead: Calcium stops at 4s^{2}. The 3d sublevel stays empty until scandium.
fields.mustwrite: Use the previous period's noble gas. Cl is in period 3, so its core is [Ne], not [Ar].

imageSubjects.aside: period 3 of a periodic table wall chart, lit from the side

slides.notes: N: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^3, 3 unpaired. Cl: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5, 1 unpaired. Ca: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2, 0 unpaired. 3d stays empty until scandium. Image prompt (aside slot): period 3 of a periodic table wall chart, lit from the side.

fields.headline: Noble-Gas Shorthand
fields.subhead: Replace the filled inner core with a noble gas in brackets.
fields.mustwrite: Use the noble gas from the previous period. Cl is in period 3, so its core is [Ne].

imageSubjects.concept: a neon sign tube glowing orange-red in a dark window

slides.notes: COMMON ERROR (brief): using the noble gas of the same period, or the element's own. Cl is period 3, so the core is [Ne], not [Ar]; the core is the previous period's noble gas. Shorthand: [Ne] 3s^2 3p^5, which equals the longhand 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5. Image prompt (concept slot): a neon sign tube glowing orange-red in a dark window.

fields.headline: Example: Iron
fields.subhead: Longhand, shorthand, and the unpaired count.
fields.problem: Write longhand and shorthand for iron. How many unpaired electrons?
fields.mustwrite: Fill 4s before 3d. We write 4s ahead of 3d.

imageSubjects.aside: a rusted iron nail on a white bench

slides.notes: Students copy the setup, then work it. Answer on the next slide. Fe, Z = 26. Fill 4s before 3d, and we write 4s ahead of 3d (filling-order notation, PROVISIONAL convention). Image prompt (aside slot): a rusted iron nail on a white bench.

fields.headline: Iron, Worked
fields.subhead: Argon is the core. Then 4s, then 3d.
fields.mustwrite: Fe is [Ar] 4s^{2} 3d^{6}. One pair and 4 singles in the 3d boxes.

slides.notes: Fe: [Ar] 4s^2 3d^6, 18 + 2 + 6 = 26. The 3d boxes hold one pair and four singles, so 4 unpaired. Longhand: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^2 3d^6.

fields.headline: Two Exceptions: Cr and Cu
fields.subhead: Learn both. The rules predict 4s^{2} for each, and the measurements disagree.
fields.a3_b: Half-full and full 3d are extra stable.

slides.notes: Only Cr and Cu are taught as exceptions. Cr: [Ar] 4s^1 3d^5. Cu: [Ar] 4s^1 3d^10. These are measured ground states, not textbook errors. PROVISIONAL label: 'half-full or full d is extra stable' is a simplification, not a predictor; it does not explain every exception. Mo, Ag and Au (one period down) are not taught and unchecked here; outside Cr and Cu, say 'look it up'.

fields.headline: Checking a Configuration
fields.subhead: Run these four checks in order.
fields.s1_b: Do the raised numbers add up to Z?
fields.s3_b: Singles first. Pairs have opposite spins.
fields.s4_b: Previous noble gas? Is it Cr or Cu?

imageSubjects.band: a teacher's red pen resting on a page of student work

slides.notes: Run the four checks in order: count, caps and order, Hund and Pauli, then core / Cr / Cu. Stop at the first failure. Image prompt (band slot): a teacher's red pen resting on a page of student work.

fields.headline: Example: Spot the Mistake
fields.subhead: Each was written as a ground state.
fields.problem: Each of these is wrong. Name the rule or fact it breaks.
fields.mustwrite: Add the electrons first. If the total is not Z, stop there.

imageSubjects.aside: a page of student work with a few lines circled in red pen

slides.notes: Answers on the next slide. Each was written as a ground state. (a) O: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 is 10 electrons, O has 8. (b) K: [Ar] 3d^1 puts 3d before 4s. (c) Ca: [Ne] 4s^2 is 12 electrons, wrong core. (d) Cr: [Ar] 4s^2 3d^4 obeys the rules but is not the real ground state. Image prompt (aside slot): a page of student work with a few lines circled in red pen.

fields.headline: Spot the Mistake, Worked
fields.subhead: Four problems, four different checks. Each fix is on the right.
fields.f1_b:
(a) Count: 10, not 8
(b) Aufbau: 4s first
(c) Core: needs [Ar]
(d) Real Cr differs
fields.mustwrite: Cr follows the rules on paper, but the measured ground state is [Ar] 4s^{1} 3d^{5}.

imageSubjects.data: a pencil resting on a page of crossed-out electron counts

slides.notes: Corrected: (a) O 1s^2 2s^2 2p^4. (b) K [Ar] 4s^1. (c) Ca [Ar] 4s^2. (d) Cr [Ar] 4s^1 3d^5. Teach 'rules-consistent' versus 'observed': (d) passes every rule on paper and is still not the real atom. Image prompt (data slot): a pencil resting on a page of crossed-out electron counts.

fields.headline: Example: Spot the Mistake, Diagrams
fields.subhead: Two orbital diagrams. Each breaks a different rule.
fields.a1_b: Only the three 2p boxes are drawn.
fields.a3_b: Name the broken rule. Redraw it correctly.

slides.notes: Orbital-diagram errors (brief items c, d), labelled (e) and (f) here. (e) N 2p drawn up, down, up: three singles but not parallel. (f) Ne 2s drawn up, up in one box: Pauli. Ask which rule each breaks and what the fix looks like.

fields.headline: Spot the Mistake, Diagrams, Worked
fields.subhead: One Hund error and one Pauli error. The fixes are drawn at left.
fields.f1_b:
(e) Hund: spins differ
(f) Pauli: same spin
fields.work:
Fixed:
(e) 2p: up, up, up
(f) 2s: up, down
fields.mustwrite: Hund: singles first, all spins the same. Pauli: two in one orbital must be opposite.

slides.notes: (e) Hund: unpaired electrons need parallel spins. Correct N 2p: up, up, up. (f) Pauli: two electrons in one orbital must have opposite spins. Correct Ne 2s: up, down. The brief's other Hund error (pair, single, empty) is the WRONG row on the Hund slide earlier in this deck.

fields.headline: Check Yourself
fields.subhead: Work all three in your notes before we compare.
fields.k2_b: Write the shorthand and sketch the 3p boxes.
fields.k3_b: Write the actual shorthand. Say why it is an exception.
fields.mustwrite: Show the electron sum for each one. If it is not Z, find the error.

imageSubjects.aside: a pencil and a blank sheet of lined paper on a lab bench

slides.notes: Answers (re-derived). P, Z = 15: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^3, 2+2+6+2+3 = 15, 3 unpaired. S, Z = 16: [Ne] 3s^2 3p^4, 10+2+4 = 16; 3p boxes: one pair and two singles, 2 unpaired. Cu, Z = 29: [Ar] 4s^1 3d^10, 18+1+10 = 29; exception, a filled 3d is extra stable (simplification, PROVISIONAL label). Image prompt (aside slot): a pencil and a blank sheet of lined paper on a lab bench.
